questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Choosing somewhere that were different from what i knew

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Met wonderful people and the city of Prague is beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most information could be found online.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not recieve any help right on arrival, but we did have orientation day the first day of school. I do know it is possible though to get a university "buddy" that potentially could assist you from day one.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Orientation day was on the first day of school, which interfered with first day of classes, so that was a little bit annoying. But it was quite informative, and the contact person at the university was quick at answering emails if I had any further questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were different dormitories you could be placed into. The one i lived in you shared a room two people and a kitchen four people. It was a little outside the main city but had good public transport connections.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Each room had an attached kitchen shared with another room. It had a tiny fridge and two burners for cooking, but plenty of cupboard space. There was also a room you could go to for an oven. It was possible to buy meals at lunch at the on campus cafeteria.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was a little small and very dirty when I got there, but my roommates tuned out to be great. We cleaned up the place and we ended up having a great time together.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The facilities themselves were okay, just dont expect too much. The best thing about it was living with other students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy in some ways, but stressful in other ways for me personally at least.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the first days of classes you get your login that enables you to register for classes. Then you have three month were you have the possibility of changing your courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to the erasmus contact person at the university, who was fairly quick at answering emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you find something you really want to sign up for, then do so as fast as possible since the courses can fill up. And once you get able to login you get more information about the courses, like whether they are BA level or MA level.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Interesting courses, but difficult to find couses not continuing from last semester.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was close to the level of KU courses, at some points more difficult but that might be because it was the first time for me doing MA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was close to how it is at home, with lectures and exercise classes, but teachers are allowed to do whatevere they want so it might vary.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: English for mathematicians NJAZ096, Czech for beginners NJAZ098, Algebraic number theory NMAG430, Nonlinear Differential Equations NMNV406, Functional Analysis for physicist NMMO302, and Groups Representations NMAG438.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked my language courses, both really interesting in different ways and with very nice teachers. Algebraic number theory I would also recommend, although it was a difficult course. Nonlinear differential equations I would really recommend, as it was very nicely self contained. I would recommend not to take functional analysis and group representations, as the first one had a really confusing exam, and the second one was very difficult.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was actually cheaper that I expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Daily groceries were cheaper, eating out cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not do any of these things

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that many hostet by the university itself, but a lot by other erasmus groups.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do events hostet by the city, like during my stay I went to Museum by night, Witch burning ceremony, concert on the river Vltava, music festival on the river islands, and more. They are fun and let you see the city in a different way.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Krakow in Poland, and although i havent been myself i heard good things about Wien and Budapest. But there is also a lot of beautiful one day trips within Czechia like Brno, Carlovy vary, Cesky krumlov, Kutna hora and more.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not too difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Like expected I ended up mostly speaking with eramus students, but the local students are a lot like danish students in that they mostly keep to themselves and for them it is business as usual, but a lot of them are also not that good at english. The ones I did speak with were very nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Going to the supermarket can be tough when everything is in czech or sometimes german.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Beautiful buildings with an appreciation for old architecture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try not to stress too much about courses before hand, they will fall into place once you get there. The best way to enjoy Prague is to just walk through the city. And dont worry too much about the classes, remember you are there to experience so much more than just the university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: How the exams unfold can be very confusing, so just be aware of that when you get towards the end of your stay.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The connections I made with other people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All of the paperwork before the exchange itself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
